title: The Mild winter on the coast
subtitle: 天气气候 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 天气气候（人与自然·自然生态·天气与气候）
meta: 主题语境：天气气候（人与自然·自然生态·天气与气候）　|　核心词汇：mild　|　正文 339 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 mild 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1960 the shopkeeper wrote of ① a mild winter on the coast in the account, and everybody in the shop said at once that it was ② milder than the one named there the year before. Three months on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the shopkeeper, who never explained anything, had done it without a word of thanks and gone home; it was the mild ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the mildest winter on the coast anybody in the shop had ever seen, or so the account for July 1954 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too mild to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the buyer who had come to help; the mild ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the scale at the far counter, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a mild fever of the child, and said that no buyer in his right mind would call it ⑥ as mild as the fever of the child they had once had in the old shop. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was mild or not, and he said so.

By 1967 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the account. What the line asked for was ⑦ something mild, and nothing besides. The buyer from the next shop called the whole plan ⑧ quite mild; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the account kept the names of the mild ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1970, at once, she wrote of another mild winter on the coast in the same account, and the work, which took two months, seemed ⑨ milder than anybody had expected. ⑩ The mildest fever of the child in the whole shop, she said in 1972, was the one she could never quite name; the mild ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 温和（前置定语 a mild winter on the coast：1960 年掌柜在账本里记下的那件温和的冬天）
B. adj. 温和／轻微（比较级 milder than：文中两处，一处比海边温和的冬天，一处比预想）
C. adj. 温和／轻微（最高级 the mildest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 温和（表语 too mild to do：母亲觉得它太温和，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 轻微（前置定语 a mild fever of the child：叔叔把整件事称作一桩轻微的发热）
F. adj. 轻微（同级比较 as mild as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩孩子轻微的发热相比）
G. adj. 轻微（后置定语 something mild：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 轻微（受程度副词修饰 quite mild：那位买主的评价）

items.q: a mild winter on the coast
the mildest winter on the coast anybody
a mild fever of the child
The mildest fever of the child in

answers.why: mild 意为“温和”，1960 年掌柜在账本里记下的是“一件温和的冬天”，此处作前置定语 a mild winter on the coast。
mild 意为“温和”，此处用比较级 milder than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
mild 意为“温和”，账本上 七月 那行字说它是铺子里最温和的一件，故用最高级 the mildest winter on the coast。
mild 意为“温和”，母亲认为这件东西“太温和了，谁也用不上”，too mild to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
mild 意为“轻微”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩轻微的发热”，此处作前置定语 a mild fever of the child。
mild 意为“轻微”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩孩子轻微的发热一样轻微”，同级比较用 as mild as。
mild 意为“轻微”，账本上那半行字要的是“轻微的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something mild。
mild 意为“轻微”，邻铺子来的那位买主认为这套计划“相当轻微”，quite 修饰原级 mild。
mild 意为“轻微”，1970 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要轻微”，故用比较级 milder than。
mild 意为“轻微”，母亲 1972 年说的是“整个铺子里最轻微的那一桩”，故用最高级 the mildest fever of the child。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1960 年，掌柜在账本里记下了一件温和的冬天。（a mild winter on the coast）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更温和。（milder than …）
母亲觉得它太温和，谁也用不上。（too mild to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩轻微的发热。（a mild fever of the child）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩孩子轻微的发热一样轻微。（as mild as …）
到了 1967 年，账本上只剩半行字：要的是一件轻微的东西。（something mild）
answers: In 1960 the shopkeeper wrote of a mild winter on the coast in the account.
Everybody said it was milder than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too mild to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a mild fever of the child.
He said nobody would call it as mild as the fever of the child they had once had.
By 1967 the account asked for nothing but something mild.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 mild 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1960 the shopkeeper wrote of a mild winter on the coast in the account, and nobody forgot it.
It was the mildest winter on the coast in the shop, or so the account says.
My mother thought it too mild to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a mild fever of the child, and nobody argued with him.
The buyer from the next shop called the plan quite mild, and everybody laughed.
The mild ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
